results.content:
That's why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta. It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what's ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.

> Eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming. Claim by January 15, 2027. Terms apply.

### How Claude Ship works: review, fix, and approve

Claude Ship is made up of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don't have to manage each step manually. [...] # Introducing Claude Ship

Open a pull request and get back to building. Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team's policy allows.

Anyone who has opened a pull request knows how this goes. They start on the next thing, and then the review comes back. So they stop, dig back into the old code, push a fix, and wait for the review to run again. Then they go find someone to approve it.

There's a good reason it works this way. Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that's easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too. [...] ## Two ways to get started

### For developers: `/ship` it from Claude Code

Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new `/ship` command in Claude Code. When a change is ready, they run `/ship`. Claude pushes it, opens the PR, reviews the change, and works on feedback and failing checks to help get it ready to merge. What can merge depends on the developer's permissions and the repository's branch rules.

Example of running /ship in Claude Code.

### For admins and engineering leaders: set the rules, one repository at a time

Turning Claude Ship on for an entire repository puts it to work across a team's pull requests automatically, under settings and an approval policy the team controls. Developers don't need to manually invoke the `/ship` command.

results.content:
But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

## What Claude Ship means for developers

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must) [...] With Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward developers who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code

More from ZDNET

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”

## How Claude Ship works [...] Developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

## How to try Claude Ship

Claude Team and Enterprise plan users can try the new feature using the /ship command now available in Claude Code. The feature uses tokens, so your overall bill may change, but it depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

# Claude Ship: Anthropic Now Lets Claude Approve Code, Too

Colorful programming code on a computer screen

Set Trending Topics as a preferred source on Google.

Claude writes the code, Claude reviews the code, and now Claude approves the code, too.

Anthropic has just unveiled Claude Ship. The new product is designed to move pull requests, the proposed changes to a codebase, automatically through review, fixes and approval. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it,” Anthropic wrote in its announcement. Claude Ship is available now in beta for customers on Team and Enterprise plans whose code lives on GitHub.

## Review, Fix, Approve [...] That makes sense, because Claude Code is Anthropic’s biggest revenue driver, as Trending Topics reported. With Claude Ship, Anthropic now covers not just writing code but the entire path to approval. Anthropic sees exactly this step as the bottleneck: When agents write most of the code, as is already the case on the Claude Code team according to Anthropic, everything after the pull request should move just as fast.

Anthropic is taking on a number of specialized competitors. GitHub also offers automated code reviews with Copilot, alongside start-ups such as CodeRabbit and Cursor with its review agent Bugbot.

## First Major Launch Since the I.P.O.
